newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Alfa-Eko gets UN approval of Iraq oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Russian Alfa-Eko gets UN approval of Iraq oil deal.

text.p: Russia's Alfa-Eko trading company said on Tuesday it had received approval from the United Nations to buy a total of 40,000 barrels per day of crude oil over six months from Iraq.

"The U.N. sent all the corresponding documents to us and Iraqi organisations involved, approving our two deals to buy 15,000 bpd and 25,000 bpd over six months," said a company official, who declined to be named.

He said the firm was planning to start shipments in January after it works out where to market the crude. The official said Alfa-Eko had plans to sell the oil in Southeast Asia, in southern Europe and in Latin America.
Company officials said last week Alfa-Eko wanted to market the oil in the United States.
The two contracts are to be lifted from Iraq's southern terminal Mina al-Bakr.
Several Russian companies are still awaiting approval from the U.N. for similar contracts.
